newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Congress opens its third and last regular session today after a two-month recess with Presisent Ramos giving his last State of the Nation Address, detailing achievements in the last five years and urging Congress to pass a vital tax bill. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Armed Forces of the Philippines is set to launch a massive operation against 10 big-time drug syndicates in the country, Brig. Gen. Benjamin Libarnes, head of military intelligence said. (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Politicians and victims of human rights abuses during the time of the late President Ferdinand Marcos support moves to allow General Fabian Ver, the former Armed Forces chief of staff, to come back to the Philippines, to face trial for the assassination of Senator Benigno Aquino Jr in August 1983. (TODAY)
- A senator has asked for police security, not once but twice for a suspected "godfather' of drug lords. (INQUIRER)

- Hundreds of Filipino Americans, some in their 70's and 80's, marched outside the White House, pleading for veterans benefits for Filipinos who served under the American flag during World War II. (MALAYA)

- Supermodel Claudia Schiffer was welcomed by fans including Philippine top models as she attended the soft opening of Fashion Cafe at the Glorietta in Makati, Manila's financial district. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Senate ways and means committee chairman Senator Juan Ponce Enrile said the committee approved its version of the remaining component of the Comprehensive Tax Reform package last Friday, deciding to lower individual income tax exemptions, but making sure of a positive fiscal balance. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- The central bank said the national government's decision to reduce its borrowings from the domestic sector to avoid paying high interest rates could even mean lower income for the state. (TODAY).

- Pressure on the badly mauled currencies of the Asian economies is unlikely to ease much in the coming days, with last week's efforts by central bankers and ministers to either frighten or reassure the markets amounting to little. (MANILA STANDARD)
- J.P. Morgan said the Philippines can withstand the pressure being caused by a volatile regional currency market becuase of its robust economy. (CHRONICLE/MALAYA)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has cleared the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) chairman Wilson Sy of insider trading and prioce manipulation, as well as violation of the broker-director rule under the Revised Securities Act. (INQUIRER)

- The United States will call on ASEAN members to put their economies in order, as the nine nations agreed Friday to intensify cooperation in a bid to stabilise their economies following recent plunges in Asian currency values. (BULLETIN)
